ingredients: 2 tablespoons (¼ stick; 30 g) butter, room temperature
1 packet (1 scant tablespoon; 7 g active dry) yeast
¾–1 cup (6–8 fl oz; 170–225 g) warm water
steps: Put all ingredients except warm water in a mixing bowl. Stir briefly to distribute the yeast; use a stand mixer with dough hook at its lowest setting or a mixing spoon.

Add half to three-quarters of the warm water and mix thoroughly until the dough comes together, several minutes in a stand mixer. Alternatively knead by hand on a clean oiled or floured surface for up to 10 minutes, adding flour or water by the spoonful as needed.

Assess the dough: if sticky and too slack to form a smooth soft ball, mix in flour a generous spoonful at a time, usually no more than ½ cup (60 g). If dry flour remains, add a little remaining warm water directly to it and mix. Correct excess water with a spoonful of flour.
Unless it is a hot day, turn on the empty cold oven for one minute, then turn it off to create a comfortably warm rising place.
Cover the dough with a lid or plate, or coat its surface with oil to prevent drying.
Put the bowl in the slightly warm oven or another warm place. Check that the oven is off.
Let rise about 1 hour until puffy and nearly doubled; cold water will require longer.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or grease it lightly.
Spread a large spoonful of flour on the work surface.
Take the dough from the oven and scrape onto the floured surface.
Roll in flour to coat lightly, adding flour to prevent sticking. Form a rough log and cut into 12 similar pieces with a sharp knife or bench scraper.
Dust wet cut edges with flour. Choose a smooth top, stretch or pinch its edges underneath, pinch the bottom closed, flatten between your hands and put seam-side down on the baking sheet.
Repeat for all pieces, spacing them an inch or two apart.
Proof in the barely warm oven for 45 minutes to an hour. If necessary warm the empty oven for 30 seconds, then turn it off before inserting the dough.
When nicely puffy, remove the baking sheet.
Preheat the empty oven to 375°F (190°C, gas mark 5).
Bake the proofed buns for 12–15 minutes until golden brown.
Serve hot, warm or at room temperature.
